buildSourceNote: Build 141 carries v1.1.0-rc.18. rc.17 and rc.18 are BOTH navigation defects the owner hit while actually using the app, and both were MINE. rc.17: Staff Activity had shipped in rc.15 with its ROLE_TABS entries, its render block and its server gate, but was never added to WORKSPACE_MAPPING in AppShell.tsx - and the sub-nav renders only tabs whose mapping equals the active workspace, so an unmapped tab matched NO workspace, appeared in no menu at all, and could only be opened by typing /staff-activity. Reported as 'where can i find staff activity'. Mapped to 'hr' and verified in the served bundle. Every other tab id in App.tsx (44 of them) was audited against the map: the only one without a mapping is 'logout-deep-link', the intentional Logout pseudo-tab, so this was a single mistake rather than a class. Note for future tabs: src/lib/tabRoutes.ts needs NO change (a tab id IS its path) but WORKSPACE_MAPPING does. rc.18: the header search input had no value, no onChange, no handler and no state - it had NEVER been wired, and typing in it did nothing. Reported as 'what use it of that search tab on the top besides back button'. It is now a jump-to-screen launcher over permittedTabs only, so it needs no new endpoint, no new permission and no data semantics, and because it can only reach screens the role already has it cannot become an access path. The broader search (job cards by number or VRN, people, vehicles) needs endpoint and matching decisions and is deliberately left open rather than half-built. Prior builds: 139 carried rc.15 and rc.16, 140 carried rc.17. rc.15 adds staff activity reporting and CORRECTS A SERIOUS ERROR OF MINE THAT HAD A SECURITY CONSEQUENCE. The owner asked 'can i also see the user activity like his compliance report, when did he login did he punched attendance, how much active he is', visible 'only to the developer and gm service and hr/admin'. NEW: GET /api/admin/user-activity/staff and /:userId, implemented in src/api/routes/user-activity.routes.ts and mounted via createUserActivityRouter (the auth helpers are closure-local in server.ts); screen StaffActivityHub.tsx at /staff-activity, registered for admin, developer and gm_service ONLY - there is NO 'hr' role in `roles`, the HR account hr_dapl carries 'admin'. Assembled from five grouped queries merged in JS rather than one wide join, because the sources key on employee_id, user_id and actor_user_id differently and a join multiplies rows, producing counts that look plausible and are wrong. Attendance queries list columns explicitly because workforce_attendance carries face_photo_in and face_photo_out as LONGTEXT base64. NEW, AND IT WAS THE ACTUAL BLOCKER: logins were never recorded, and login_history could NEVER have recorded them - user_id is NOT NULL with an FK to `users`, but the app authenticates against user_access_master and only 19 of 61 accounts exist in `users`. The HR/admin account (29), the security agent (45), the biller (50) and the advisor (95) are ALL absent from `users`, so every insert would have failed with ER_NO_REFERENCED_ROW. Migration 32 (login_history_relax_fk) drops that FK and adds idx_login_history_user_time. /api/auth/login and /api/auth/verify-otp now record success AND failure, and the write never throws - an audit side-effect must not deny a valid user access. There is NO BACKFILL, deliberately: past sign-ins are unrecoverable, so last_login_at is null for almost everyone until they sign in once, and the UI says 'Never recorded' with a banner rather than inventing history. THE ERROR: in rc.13 I added 'reception' to GATE_OUT_SECURITY_ROLES while stating that production had ZERO security_agent accounts. THAT WAS FALSE. suryakant (user 45) is an active security_agent with a valid bcrypt password and must_change_password 0. My probe counted security users through a LEFT JOIN onto `roles` and returned 0, and I trusted that count without querying the account table directly - a zero from a join is evidence about the join, not about the world. The consequence was real: a front-desk role was handed the ability to RELEASE A VEHICLE. The true defect was never a missing account - security_agent was ALREADY in GATE_OUT_SECURITY_ROLES, so the API always accepted it, but ROLE_TABS.security_agent had no security-workspace tab, and the only caller of POST /api/gate-out/gate-out in the whole repository is SecurityWorkspace.tsx:63, rendered solely on that tab id. The role held the authority and could not exercise it. rc.15 gives security_agent AND gate_personnel the tab, and REMOVES 'reception' from both GATE_OUT_SECURITY_ROLES and ROLE_TABS.reception. The journey is unaffected: the GM (sayeed_dp) holds security-workspace and cashier-workspace. ALSO FIXED in rc.15: EmployeePerformanceHub's 'Completed' column read 0 for every employee forever, because it compared job_status to the literal 'completed', which the enum cannot hold; it now uses isWorkCompleteStatus(), and the name match is trimmed and case-insensitive because production stores names like 'ranjeet ' with a trailing space. rc.16 fixes a defect ONLY LIVE TESTING COULD REVEAL: the first recorded login carried ip_address 169.254.169.126, a link-local internal hop, because Express with trust proxy 1 resolves req.ip to the LAST X-Forwarded-For entry while Cloud Run puts the real client FIRST. It now takes the leftmost entry, and the comment records that the value is a client-supplied claim which must never drive an authorisation or rate-limiting decision. See docs/CHANGELOG.md.

NOTE FOR ANYONE READING THE TRAIL: those two 'failed' rows for suryakant (user 45) are the author's verification attempts, not an attack. STILL OPEN, PRODUCTION-WIDE, FOUND WHILE VERIFYING rc.14: the rc1 workforce profile never applies. .dockerignore and .gcloudignore both exclude '.env' and '.env.*', and .env.rc1 is gitignored as well, so VITE_WORKFORCE_PROFILE is undefined at build time and every 'import.meta.env.VITE_WORKFORCE_PROFILE === rc1' check in the codebase is permanently false - the App.tsx tab guard AND AttendanceShiftLog.tsx. Confirmed against the live bundle: zero occurrences of 'rc1', zero of 'dev', and the excluded-tabs array literal absent. Net effect today is permissive (nothing is hidden), so it is NOT an outage, but it means the production-hardening configuration is documentation rather than behaviour. Needs an OWNER DECISION: either pass VITE_WORKFORCE_PROFILE via a Docker ARG/ENV or a Cloud Build substitution so it survives the context exclusion, or accept that rc1 is inert and delete the dead checks. '.env.*' must stay dockerignored either way - excluding env files from the image is the right instinct, and .env.rc1 merely happens to carry no secret.
